Purpose and exclusions

Mining and woodcutting share one validated action/claim pipeline but use different tool, animation, profession and yield definitions. Two clients contesting one node cannot both receive its exclusive depleted-generation reward.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create DA_GatherRule_Mining and DA_GatherRule_Woodcutting with tool tags, durations, yield tables and profession IDs. Add corresponding material definitions created in Phase 09.
  2. Add URPGGatheringComponent once to BP_PlayerCharacter and expose RequestGather/CancelGather as guarded custom commands.
  3. Configure BP_ResourceNode with source identity, resource definition and interaction interface; it does not own a copy of player inventory.
  4. Assign WBP_Gathering to ScreenRouter's nonmodal progress layer. Show target, progress, cancel prompt and structured rejection; input remains responsive but movement cancels under default rule.
  5. Reopen resource director to consume committed depletion, inventory service to plan yield capacity, profession component to apply receipt XP, and PaperZD mappings for mining/chopping p2 only after actual archive audit.
  6. Test both clients against one node, one full inventory, one missing tool, one moving player and a backend response dropped after commit.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
RequestGather(CommandId, NodeActor, ExpectedGeneration) -> Started|ResourceBusy|WrongTool|SkillRequiredNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
CancelGather(ActionId, Reason) -> Canceled|AlreadyTerminalNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
CompleteGather(ActionId) -> GrantReceipt|NodeDepleted|NoSpace|Interrupted; server timer onlyNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ObserveGatherState(ActionId) -> ProgressAndReason; local/replicated presentationNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Mining and woodcutting with exclusive claims. Rule owner: URPGGatheringComponent. This asset’s role is Mining and woodcutting share one validated action/claim pipeline but use different tool, animation, profession and yield definitions. Two clients contesting one node cannot both receive its exclusive depleted-generation reward.

  1. Character_A and Character_B press Interact on OreSite_A01. Server checks range/LOS, active generation, pickaxe ownership, mining skill and action state.
  2. The zone serializes reservation acquisition: A wins; B receives ResourceBusy and no materials/XP. Reservations expire/cancel safely if A moves away.
  3. Server advances a 3-second mining action. The p2 tool pose is cosmetic; a missing/late hit-frame notify cannot finish the action or award ore.
  4. At completion repeat tool/range/alive/generation checks and capacity plan. Backend transaction locks node generation and character, marks depleted, grants resolved ore plus mining XP and stores receipt atomically.
  5. After commit replicate node depletion to both clients, update A's inventory/profession UI, and schedule persisted respawn. B's subsequent request receives NodeDepleted.
  6. For TreeSite_W03 repeat with Axe, woodcutting profession, biome-specific AshLog yields and chopping visual mapping. Invalid terrain sites are never spawned.
  7. On timeout after commit, quarantine that action/node from conflicting mutations and reconcile the original receipt. Restart reads depleted state; no second grant.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / OreSite_A01 / TreeSite_W03 / Character_A / Character_B. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Two simultaneous starts -> one reservation; one ResourceBusy.
A cancels/moves/dies -> reservation released, no materials/XP; B can start if node remains active.
Completion races with stale generation -> NodeDepleted/StaleGeneration, no grant.
Full bag -> NoSpace before depletion commit; node stays active and reservation releases.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
